title: Measles Cases Climb. Stocks Recover Ground. Iran Talks Continue.
subject: Measles Cases Climb. Stocks Recover Ground. Iran Talks Continue.
preview_text: The latest health count, a divided market and a new White House chief of staff.
description: Measles cases exceed 5,000, technology shares regain ground and new U.S. strikes come as Qatar continues Iran mediation.
contents_extra: Rocket engines, the White House transition, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Measles Cases Pass 5,000 Across Most of the U.S.
paragraphs: The United States has recorded 5,182 confirmed measles cases so far this year, according to the latest CDC data. Al Jazeera reports that this is the highest annual count since 1991. Cases have been confirmed in 45 states and Washington, D.C., ABC News reports.

About 96% of cases involve people who were unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown, according to ABC’s review of CDC figures. Al Jazeera reports a dispute over classifying measles deaths, leaving federal and state totals different. The latest data also show lower kindergarten vaccination coverage than before the pandemic.

stories.title: Technology Shares Rebound Without Erasing the Week’s Losses
paragraphs: Technology stocks regained some ground Friday after a sharp selloff, but Wall Street still ended the week lower. Reuters reports that the Nasdaq gained about 1.1% while the Dow fell 0.46%. Chipmakers led the rebound, following worries about AI infrastructure spending and possible tighter regulation.

The recovery was uneven across regions and indexes. Reuters reports that the Nasdaq posted a fourth weekly decline. Investors also weighed stronger U.S. hiring data and the outlook for interest rates. A positive session for some technology shares did not resolve concerns about the cost of the AI buildout.

photo.alt: New York Stock Exchange facade; file photo

stories.title: New U.S. Strikes Come as Qatar Keeps Iran Mediation Active
paragraphs: Trump said U.S. forces carried out limited strikes against an Iranian air defense system Friday. AP reports that Iranian state media described explosions on Qeshm Island, near the Strait of Hormuz. Trump described the action as minor but did not provide detailed information about the target.

Diplomacy continued alongside the military action. Al Jazeera reports that Qatar rejected claims that negotiations had failed on Saturday. Qatar’s prime minister said mediation remained active to prevent further escalation. Neither those statements nor Trump’s claims of progress establish that the parties have reached an agreement.

stories.title: AST Buys Engine Capacity While Keeping Other Launch Providers
paragraphs: AST SpaceMobile is moving into rocket development with a Firefly engine agreement worth more than $1.3 billion. Reuters reports that Blacklift would support AST’s satellite broadband network. The planned vehicle could carry five BlueBird satellites, with a debut targeted for late 2028 rather than an announced launch date.

The purchase is not a complete break with existing launch companies. Reuters describes the deal as a bid for more reliable access to space. AST says it still has more than 100 outside launch agreements. Firefly will supply engines initially, while licensing lets AST eventually manufacture them itself.

deep_dive.title: What Miller’s Promotion Changes Inside the White House
paragraphs: What happened. Trump selected Stephen Miller to succeed Susie Wiles as chief of staff, with the change taking effect Monday. ABC reports that Wiles will move to Trump’s political operation. Miller currently serves as deputy chief of staff for policy. His promotion follows Republican losses that will put Democrats in control of Congress.

Why it matters. The chief of staff coordinates the president’s team and helps shape access and priorities. Miller also brings extensive policy experience. AP describes his knowledge of executive power and federal government. His appointment puts an architect of Trump’s immigration program at the center of the administration as congressional scrutiny is expected to increase.

What each side says. Trump praised Wiles, who said her commitment to his agenda would continue. Democratic Rep. Robert Garcia criticized Miller’s appointment as doubling down on policies voters had rejected. AP reports those contrasting reactions after Tuesday’s Republican defeat. Miller spent the campaign defending Trump’s policies, while Wiles helped run his successful 2024 campaign.

What comes next. Miller begins Monday, as Democrats prepare to control both chambers of Congress next year. AP reports that Garcia is set to chair the House Oversight Committee. Miller’s background includes service as a homeland security adviser and coordination across federal agencies. Those roles add to his experience implementing immigration policy before this move into staff leadership.

trivia.question: Which index gained about 1.1% in Friday’s trading?
trivia.explanation: A. Nasdaq Composite. Reuters reports that it rose about 1.1% while the Dow declined.

World view: Paraguay installs a successor. Pedro Alliana became president after Santiago Peña’s impeachment over alleged links to a banking scandal; Reuters reports.
Europe checks broadcaster threats. Evacuations disrupted television programming, with no bombs found at the affected sites; Reuters reports.
Brazil building collapse injures four. Authorities said all 35 people inside a São Paulo commercial building were rescued; Reuters reports.
Germany considers a presidential candidate. German media say Merz’s party backs Ilse Aigner, who would be the first woman elected president; Reuters reports.
Need to know: Cornell faculty challenge leaders. A no confidence resolution criticized the handling of a sexual assault crisis but carries no concrete consequences; Reuters reports.
Vitamin K refusals draw scrutiny. Two studies found rising dangerous infant bleeding alongside increased refusal of protective newborn doses; Reuters reports.
Hospitals prepare for pressure. U.S. operators anticipate revenue challenges from insurance coverage losses and Medicaid funding changes; Reuters reports.
FDA examines gene therapy risk. The agency is investigating tumor formation associated with Novartis’ Zolgensma after two reported cases; Reuters reports.
Money & markets: Humana lifts profit guidance. Lower medical costs supported the insurer’s stronger annual forecast; Reuters reports.
Lilly reaches a telehealth agreement. Hims & Hers will offer Lilly obesity medicines directly rather than send patients to a separate platform; Reuters reports.
Dental startup targets a listing. Switzerland’s vVardis is seeking a valuation of up to $4.37 billion in a U.S. offering; Reuters reports.
Cigna raises annual forecast. The health company cited growth in insurance, specialty pharmacy and health services; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: Octopuses adapt to tighter gaps. Scientists mapped changing movement strategies that could inform robots designed for confined spaces; Reuters reports.
Ancient cannabis evidence emerges. Researchers found seeds and chemical traces in human hair at a Siberian burial site; Reuters reports.
An unusual beak gets examined. Research describes how an endangered Hawaiian honeycreeper uses its body and beak to find larvae; Reuters reports.
China adopts Antarctic legislation. The new law covers scientific activities and environmental protection in the region; Reuters reports.
The score: Lakers beat Portland 124 to 118. Luka Doncic’s 53 points included a long heave before halftime; AP reports.
Arizona defeats TCU 29 to 28. A field goal with 39 seconds left followed a recovered onside kick; AP reports.
New Mexico beats Nevada 31 to 3. The Lobos won their first game after entering the AP rankings; AP reports.
UConn tops Michigan 85 to 77. Braylon Mullins scored 23 points in the NCAA championship rematch; AP reports.
Life & culture: A Syrian journey reaches the screen. One in a Million follows refugee Israa over a decade and across eight countries; Reuters reports.
A director revisits childhood. Takashi Yamazaki’s Godzilla Minus Zero brings monster destruction to his hometown of Matsumoto; Reuters reports.
Club Kid reveals another side. Jordan Firstman says his directorial debut reflects his more sensitive and emotional personality; Reuters reports.
A familiar cat gets new company. The animated Cat in the Hat combines Dr. Seuss’s story with additional characters; Reuters reports.
